prompt.en: Which of the following is NOT one of the characteristics of Symbolic AI listed in the lecture?
prompt.zh: 下面哪一项不是课件列出的符号 AI（Symbolic AI）的特点？

options.en: Problems that have well-defined rules
options.zh: 问题有明确的规则

options.en: Reasoning that follows rules of logic
options.zh: 推理遵循逻辑规则

options.en: Solutions that are learned from large amounts of data
options.zh: 解是从大量数据里学出来的

options.en: Solutions that are provably correct when they are found
options.zh: 解一旦找到，就能被证明是正确的

options.en: Generally high explainability
options.zh: 可解释性通常很高

explain.zh: 课件 p.5 列了符号 AI 的四个特点：问题有明确的规则（well-defined rules）、推理遵循逻辑规则（rules of logic）、解一旦找到就能被证明正确（provably correct when they are found）、可解释性（**explainability**）通常很高。“从大量数据里学出解”不在其中。p.6 说得很清楚：Symbolic AI needs rules to work. Other methods (i.e. Machine Learning) need data. 从数据里学是机器学习（**Machine Learning**）的做法。其余四个选项都是课件原话，所以都不能选。
explain.en: Learning from data describes Machine Learning. Symbolic AI needs rules; the other four options are the four characteristics on p.5.

prompt.en: Which of the following problems does the lecture list as well-suited to Symbolic AI? (Select all that apply.)
prompt.zh: 下面哪些问题是课件列出的“适合符号 AI”的问题？（多选）

options.en: Finding the best move in a puzzle or game
options.zh: 找出谜题或游戏里的最佳一步

options.en: Given its values for the last month, predicting how a stock will perform in the future
options.zh: 根据一只股票上个月的数据，预测它以后的表现

options.en: Scheduling a collection of tasks so that none of them overlap
options.zh: 安排一批任务，让它们互不重叠

options.en: Given 1000 photos of dogs, determining if there is a dog in a new picture
options.zh: 看过 1000 张狗的照片后，判断一张新照片里有没有狗

options.en: Determining a robot's most likely position based on its sensor readings
options.zh: 根据传感器读数，判断机器人最可能在哪个位置

options.en: Chatting with users while playing the role of a customer service representative
options.zh: 扮演客服代表和用户聊天

explain.zh: 课件 p.6 给了 3 个适合、3 个不适合的例子。适合的三个（找最佳一步、排任务不重叠、判断机器人位置）都有明确的规则，可以按规则一步步推理。不适合的三个（预测股票、认狗、当客服聊天）写不出清楚的规则，要靠从数据里找规律。记住 p.6 那句：Symbolic AI needs rules to work. Other methods (i.e. Machine Learning) need data. 易错点：“机器人位置”听起来像要数据，但课件把它列为适合；“1000 张照片”里有数字，但它恰恰说明这个问题靠数据，不靠规则。
explain.en: p.6: the best move, scheduling tasks and a robot's most likely position are well-suited; the stock, dog-photo and customer-service problems need data, not rules.

prompt.en: According to the lecture, Symbolic AI needs data to work, while other methods such as Machine Learning need rules.
prompt.zh: 按课件的说法：符号 AI 需要数据才能工作，而机器学习等其他方法需要规则。

explain.zh: 错，正好说反了。课件 p.6 原话：Symbolic AI needs rules to work. Other methods (i.e. Machine Learning) need data. 符号 AI 要规则（比如游戏规则），机器学习要数据（比如 1000 张狗的照片）。考试遇到这种“把两边对调”的句子要特别小心。
explain.en: False: Symbolic AI needs rules; Machine Learning needs data (p.6).

prompt.en: Define Symbolic AI. Then explain why the problem 'Given 1000 photos of dogs, determine if there is a dog in a new picture' is not well-suited to Symbolic AI.
prompt.zh: 给符号 AI（Symbolic AI）下定义。然后解释：为什么“看过 1000 张狗的照片后，判断新照片里有没有狗”这个问题不适合用符号 AI？

modelAnswer.en: Symbolic AI is a sub-field of Artificial Intelligence in which problem solutions are found by encoding knowledge as symbols and then reasoning with those symbols. Recognizing a dog in a picture is not well-suited to it, because we cannot write well-defined rules that describe exactly what a dog looks like. Symbolic AI needs rules to work, while other methods, such as Machine Learning, need data, like the 1000 dog photos.
modelAnswer.zh: 第一句写定义（课件 p.5 原话）；第二句说原因：“狗长什么样”写不成明确的规则；第三句点出对比：符号 AI 要规则，机器学习要数据。

points.en: Definition: solutions are found by encoding knowledge as symbols and reasoning with those symbols.
points.zh: 定义：把知识编码成符号，再用这些符号推理来找解

points.en: Symbolic AI needs problems with well-defined rules.
points.zh: 符号 AI 需要规则明确的问题

points.en: We cannot write clear rules for what a dog looks like.
points.zh: “狗长什么样”写不成清楚的规则

points.en: This problem needs data (Machine Learning) instead of rules.
points.zh: 这种问题要靠数据（机器学习），而不是规则

explain.zh: 得分关键：定义要写全两个动作，encoding knowledge as symbols 和 reasoning with those symbols；原因要扣住“规则 vs 数据”。常见失分：只写“因为太难了”，没有说出“没有明确的规则”。

prompt.en: In the Sokoban activity, the slides show the person moving up, down, up, down, up, down, ... over and over. What do the slides call this sequence, and why?
prompt.zh: 推箱子（Sokoban）活动里，课件展示了人一直 up, down, up, down…… 来回走。课件把这串动作叫什么？为什么？

options.en: A dead-end, because a box has been pushed somewhere it can never leave
options.zh: 死路（dead-end），因为有箱子被推到了再也出不来的地方

options.en: A solution, because every move in the sequence is a legal move
options.zh: 一个解（solution），因为这串动作的每一步都是合法的

options.en: A terminal state, because the game is over and nobody can move
options.zh: 终止状态（terminal state），因为游戏结束了，谁都不能再动

options.en: A waste of time, because the same states keep repeating and no box ever moves
options.zh: 浪费时间（a waste of time），因为同样的状态反复出现，箱子一次也没动

explain.zh: 课件 p.16 的标题就是 A waste of time：人只在左边一列的中间格和上面格之间来回走，箱子一次都没动，同样的两个状态一直重复，离目标一点都没有更近。死路（dead-end）是 p.15 的另一种情况：箱子被推到动不了的位置，以后再也解不出来。“解”必须真的把所有箱子推到目标点上，光是“每步合法”不够。“终止状态”指游戏已经结束的节点，这里游戏根本没结束。这也提醒我们：穷举搜索会傻傻地生成这种重复状态，浪费时间。
explain.en: p.16 calls it 'a waste of time': the person only walks between two squares, so the same states repeat and no box moves. It is not a dead-end (p.15), not a solution, and the game is not over.

prompt.en: According to the lecture, what are a game's dynamics?
prompt.zh: 按课件，游戏的动态（dynamics）是什么？

options.en: The rules: which actions can be taken in a state and how the state changes
options.zh: 规则：在一个状态下能做哪些动作，以及状态会怎么变

options.en: A snapshot of the game at a particular moment, which we save to resume later
options.zh: 游戏在某一时刻的快照，存下来以后可以接着玩

options.en: A test that gives a T/F result to tell us whether a state has been won
options.zh: 对一个状态给出 T/F、告诉我们是否已经赢了的测试

options.en: A description of how the game begins, before any action is taken
options.zh: 对游戏如何开始（还没做任何动作时）的描述

explain.zh: p.17 原话：A game's dynamics are the rules of the game. For any given state, they tell us what actions can be taken and how the state changes when they are. 其他三个都是本课别的概念，最容易混：“快照”是状态（**state**）；“给出 T/F 的测试”是目标测试（**goal test**）；“游戏如何开始”是初始状态（**initial state**）。电脑要做搜索，这四样都要知道。
explain.en: Dynamics are the rules (p.17). The snapshot is the state, the T/F test is the goal test, and how the game begins is the initial state.

prompt.en: Discuss: What are the state and dynamics of Sokoban? Answer in 3-5 short sentences.
prompt.zh: 讨论题：推箱子（Sokoban）的状态（state）和动态（dynamics）分别是什么？用 3–5 句简短的英文回答。

modelAnswer.en: The state of Sokoban is the position of the person and the position of every box. This is the information I would have to save to put the game away and resume it later. (The walls and goal squares never move, so they only need to be saved once with the level.) The dynamics are the rules: in any state, the person can move up, down, left or right by one square. Walking into a box pushes it one square if the square behind it is free, but boxes cannot be pulled or pushed into a wall or another box.
modelAnswer.zh: 状态 = 人的位置 + 每个箱子的位置（墙和目标点固定不动，跟着关卡存一次就够了），也就是 p.17 的判断法：收起游戏、下次接着玩要存的信息。动态 = 规则：能做哪些动作（上下左右走一格），做了以后状态怎么变（走向箱子就把它推一格；不能拉，也不能推进墙或另一个箱子）。

points.en: State: the positions of the person and of every box.
points.zh: 状态：人和每个箱子的位置

points.en: The state is what you must save to resume the game later (a snapshot).
points.zh: 状态 = 下次接着玩要存的信息（快照）

points.en: Dynamics: the actions allowed in each state (move up, down, left or right).
points.zh: 动态：每个状态下能做的动作（上下左右）

points.en: Dynamics: how the state changes (a box is pushed one square; no pulling, no pushing into a wall or another box).
points.zh: 动态：状态怎么变（箱子被推一格；不能拉，不能推进墙或别的箱子）

explain.zh: 这是 p.17 的 Discuss 原题（课件把 Sokoban 拼成了 Sokobon），课件没给答案。写的时候分两半：先写 state（是什么 + 为什么是这些信息），再写 dynamics（有哪些动作 + 状态怎么变）。注意：推箱子的规则课件没写成文字，是从 p.14–16 的图里看出来的，用自己的话写清楚即可。常见错误：把 dynamics 写成“游戏的目标”（那是 goal test），或者把 state 写成“规则”。

prompt.en: Which of the following describes an exhaustive search?
prompt.zh: 下面哪一项描述的是穷举搜索（exhaustive search）？

options.en: It is an advanced search that goes deeper by ignoring parts of the tree known to be bad.
options.zh: 它是一种高级搜索：忽略树里已知不好的部分，从而搜得更深。

options.en: It considers all possibilities from the current game state until the end of the game.
options.zh: 从当前状态开始考虑所有可能，一直到游戏结束。

options.en: It generates states only to a fixed depth and gives the bottom row heuristic values.
options.zh: 只生成到固定深度，并给最底一排打启发式分。

options.en: It learns which moves are good by studying a large set of example games played before.
options.zh: 研究大量以前下过的对局，从中学出哪些走法好。

explain.zh: p.19 原话：An exhaustive search is the most basic kind of search. It considers all possibilities from the current game state until the end of the game. 其他选项：“忽略已知不好的部分”是 p.28 提到的更高级的搜索方法，课件说明 outside the scope of this class；“固定深度 + 启发式”是 p.57 为了省时间的做法，恰恰不是“考虑所有可能、直到结束”；“从例子里学”是机器学习的思路，不是搜索。
explain.en: p.19 definition. Ignoring bad parts of the tree is an advanced method (out of scope), stopping at a fixed depth is the heuristic approach of p.57, and learning from examples is Machine Learning.

prompt.en: In a state tree, what is an edge?
prompt.zh: 在状态树里，边（edge）是什么？

options.en: A state of the game at one moment in time; it is drawn as a board in the tree
options.zh: 游戏某一时刻的一个状态，在树里画成一张棋盘图

options.en: The first (topmost) node in the tree; it shows the current game state
options.zh: 树里第一个（最上面的）节点，表示当前的游戏状态

options.en: An action connecting two nodes; it goes from a parent node to a child node
options.zh: 连接两个节点的动作，从父节点指向子节点

options.en: A node in which the game is over; it never has any children
options.zh: 游戏已经结束的节点，永远没有孩子

explain.zh: p.21：each action connecting nodes is also called an edge；Each edge goes from a parent node to a child node. 其他选项都是别的术语：“某一时刻的状态”是节点（**node**）；“最上面的节点”是根节点（**root node**）；“游戏结束的节点”是终止状态（**terminal state**）。在 p.20 的图里，写着 up、down、right 的箭头就是边。
explain.en: An edge is an action connecting nodes (p.21). The other options describe a node, the root node and a terminal state.

prompt.en: Terminal states never have children, and every terminal state is a goal state.
prompt.zh: 终止状态永远没有孩子，而且每个终止状态都是目标状态。

explain.zh: 错。前半句对，后半句错。p.21 原话：Terminal states never have children and may or may not be goal states. 终止状态只说明“游戏结束了”，结局可能是赢、输或平局。例如井字棋例子（p.34）最底下 6 个终止状态里，只有 2 个是 X 赢（Goal!），另外 4 个是平局：它们是终止状态，但不是目标状态。
explain.en: False: terminal states may or may not be goal states (p.21). In the Tic-Tac-Toe tree, four terminal states are draws.

prompt.en: In a single-player puzzle, why can exhaustive search stop as soon as it finds a goal state?
prompt.zh: 在单人谜题里，为什么穷举搜索一找到目标状态就可以停下？

options.en: Because the path from the root to it is already a solution that is guaranteed to be correct
options.zh: 因为从根到它的动作路径已经是一个解，而且保证正确

options.en: Because exhaustive search is only allowed to build trees down to a depth of 3
options.zh: 因为穷举搜索只允许画到深度 3

options.en: Because a goal state is always the deepest node, so there is nothing left to draw
options.zh: 因为目标状态总是最深的节点，下面已经没什么可画了

options.en: Because exhaustive search only needs some solution, even one that may turn out to be wrong
options.zh: 因为穷举搜索只要随便一个解就行，哪怕它可能是错的

explain.zh: p.23 的 Discuss 问的就是这个，答案在 p.26：When a goal state is found, the path of actions from the root to the goal state gives the solution to the puzzle. Importantly, this solution is guaranteed to be correct! 单人谜题里每一步都由我们控制，所以找到了就够了，不用再搜剩下的树。其他选项：“深度 3”只是 p.24 活动的要求，不是穷举搜索的限制；目标状态不一定是树里最深的节点，别的分支还可以继续往下长，停下的原因是“已经有解了”；找到的解不会“可能是错的”，它保证正确（p.26），这正是可以停的原因。
explain.en: p.26: the path from the root to the goal state is a solution and is guaranteed to be correct. Depth 3 was only the activity's limit, and the goal state does not have to be the deepest node.

prompt.en:
Use exhaustive search on this Sokoban puzzle (P = person, B = box, G = goal, . = empty square; the grid has 3 rows and 2 columns):
`. .`
`P B`
`. G`
The person moves one square up, down, left or right. Walking into a box pushes it one square if the square behind it is free, and nothing can move off the grid. Which action sequences lead from the root to a node at depth 2? (Select all that apply.)
prompt.zh:
对下面这道推箱子题做穷举搜索（P = 人，B = 箱子，G = 目标点，. = 空格；3 行 2 列）：
`. .`
`P B`
`. G`
人每次上下左右走一格；走向箱子时，如果箱子后面是空格，就把它推一格；任何东西都不能离开格子。哪些动作序列能从根走到深度 2 的节点？（多选）

options.en: up, down
options.zh: up, down（先上，再下）

options.en: right, down
options.zh: right, down（先右，再下）

options.en: up, right
options.zh: up, right（先上，再右）

options.en: down, up
options.zh: down, up（先下，再上）

options.en: up, left
options.zh: up, left（先上，再左）

options.en: down, right
options.zh: down, right（先下，再右）

explain.zh: 这就是 p.24 的活动，答案树在 p.25。根状态下：up（上面是空格）合法，down（下面是空格）合法；right 会把箱子推出右边界，不合法；left 会走出左边界，不合法。所以根只有 up、down 两个孩子，任何以 right 开头的序列都不存在。up 之后人在左上角：down、right 合法，left 和 up 都会出界，所以 up, left 不存在。down 之后人在左下角：up、right（走到目标点上）合法。所以深度 2 正好 4 个节点：up-down、up-right、down-up、down-right（2 × 2 = 4）。注意 up-down、down-up 走回了和根一样的局面，但穷举搜索照样把它们画出来。
explain.en: From the root only up and down are legal (right pushes the box off the grid, left leaves the grid). After up: down or right. After down: up or right. So the depth-2 nodes are up-down, up-right, down-up and down-right.

prompt.en: When exhaustive search is applied to the Sokoban puzzle in the state tree activity, every state has exactly 2 legal actions. If you draw the state tree from the root (depth 0) down to depth 3, how many nodes does the tree contain in total?
prompt.zh: 在状态树活动的推箱子题里做穷举搜索，每个状态正好有 2 个合法动作。把状态树从根（深度 0）画到深度 3，整棵树一共有多少个节点？

explain.zh:
一层一层数，每层是上一层的 2 倍：
深度 0：1 个（根）
深度 1：1 × 2 = 2 个
深度 2：2 × 2 = 4 个
深度 3：4 × 2 = 8 个
合计 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 个，和 p.25 的答案树一致。常见错误：只数最底层（8）；算成 3 × 2 = 6；忘了算根节点（14）。
explain.en: 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 nodes (depths 0 to 3).

prompt.en: In a single-player puzzle, when exhaustive search finds a goal state, the path of actions from the root to that goal state is a solution that is guaranteed to be correct.
prompt.zh: 在单人谜题里，穷举搜索找到目标状态后，从根到这个目标状态的动作路径就是一个保证正确的解。

explain.zh: 对。p.26：When a goal state is found, the path of actions from the root to the goal state gives the solution to the puzzle. Importantly, this solution is guaranteed to be correct! 例如 p.25 的树里 up → right → down 到达 Goal!，解就是 up, right, down。注意前提是“单人谜题”：到了两人游戏（p.32），找到目标状态就不再保证能赢了。
explain.en: True (p.26). This guarantee holds for single-player puzzles; in two-player games a goal state no longer guarantees a win.

prompt.en: Describe the goal of Search and explain how exhaustive search builds a state tree and finds a solution for a single-player puzzle such as Sokoban. Then explain how exhaustive search differs from the way a human thinks about the same puzzle.
prompt.zh: 说明搜索（Search）的目标，并解释穷举搜索如何为推箱子这样的单人谜题画出状态树、找到解。然后说明穷举搜索和人思考同一道题的方式有什么不同。

modelAnswer.en: Search is a method for a computer to 'look ahead' by using the game's dynamics to generate possible future states. Its goal is to find a goal state, where the goal test gives T, and the actions that lead to it. Exhaustive search, the most basic kind of search, adds the current game state as the root node. Then it considers all legal actions, draws the resulting states as children, and repeats this for every child, one level at a time. It stops when a goal state is found or when there are no more children to generate. The path of actions from the root to the goal state is the solution, for example up, right, down in the lecture's tree, and it is guaranteed to be correct. A human thinks differently: we use intuition, ignore moves that are clearly useless and avoid dead ends. Exhaustive search does not understand the puzzle, so it blindly generates every state, even repeated ones, which wastes time.
modelAnswer.zh: 结构：① 搜索的定义（p.19 原话）+ 目标：找到目标状态和通往它的动作；② 穷举搜索的步骤（p.23）：当前状态作根 → 所有合法动作的结果画成孩子 → 对每个孩子重复 → 找到目标状态或没有孩子可生成时停；③ 读解（p.26）：根到目标状态的路径，例如 up, right, down，保证正确；④ 和人对比（p.24 的 Discuss）：人靠直觉、跳过没用的走法、避开死路；穷举搜索不理解题目，机械地把所有状态（包括重复的）都生成出来，浪费时间。

points.en: Search looks ahead by using the dynamics to generate possible future states.
points.zh: 搜索 = 用动态（规则）生成未来可能的状态，往前看

points.en: The goal is to reach a goal state (the goal test gives T).
points.zh: 目标：找到目标状态（目标测试给 T）

points.en: Exhaustive search steps: the current state is the root, add children for all legal actions, repeat level by level, stop at a goal state or when no children are left.
points.zh: 穷举搜索步骤：当前状态作根，所有合法动作的结果作孩子，一层层重复，找到目标状态或没有孩子时停

points.en: The solution is the path of actions from the root to the goal state, and it is guaranteed to be correct.
points.zh: 解 = 根到目标状态的动作路径，保证正确

points.en: Humans use intuition and skip useless moves and dead ends; exhaustive search blindly checks everything, including repeated states.
points.zh: 人靠直觉，跳过没用的走法和死路；穷举搜索机械地全部检查，包括重复状态

explain.zh: 这题对应学习目标 2（Describe the goal of Search and draw an exhaustive Search Tree）和 p.24 的 Discuss。课件没有一句话直接写“搜索的目标是……”，把 p.18–19、p.23、p.26 的内容组合起来说即可。如果考试要求“画树”，记住：根写在最上面，每条边标上动作名，每一层画出所有合法动作的结果，重复的局面也要画。

prompt.en: According to the lecture, what makes Search hard?
prompt.zh: 按课件，是什么让搜索变难？

options.en: The goal test is too hard to compute for most states, so wins are missed.
options.zh: 大多数状态的目标测试太难算，所以会漏掉赢的局面。

options.en: Solutions found by exhaustive search are often incorrect and must be checked.
options.zh: 穷举搜索找到的解经常是错的，还得再检查。

options.en: In every game an opponent blocks our moves, so a goal state is never reached.
options.zh: 每个游戏都有对手挡路，所以永远到不了目标状态。

options.en: The number of nodes grows exponentially with depth, and each state costs time.
options.zh: 节点数随深度指数增长，而且每生成一个状态都要花时间。

explain.zh: p.27–28：the number of nodes grows exponentially with depth；Each state generated costs the computer time, and exponential growth is fast；This exponential growth is what makes Search hard. 其他选项都和课件矛盾：目标测试对任何状态都能给出 T/F（p.18），难的不是它；找到的解保证正确（p.26）；对手挡路是多人游戏里“找到目标状态也不保证赢”的原因（p.32），不是搜索难的原因，而且推箱子这样的单人谜题根本没有对手。
explain.en: p.28: exponential growth is what makes Search hard. The goal test always gives T/F, found solutions are guaranteed correct, and single-player puzzles have no opponent.

prompt.en: In the lecture's Sokoban state tree, 2 actions were possible from every state, so the number of nodes doubled at each depth (depth 0 has 1 node, depth 1 has 2, depth 2 has 4). If this pattern continues, exactly how many nodes would be at depth 10?
prompt.zh: 课件的推箱子状态树里，每个状态都有 2 个动作，所以每往下一层，节点数翻一倍（深度 0 有 1 个，深度 1 有 2 个，深度 2 有 4 个）。照这个规律，深度 10 正好会有多少个节点？

explain.zh: 深度 d 的节点数 = 2 × 2 × …… × 2（d 个 2）= 2^d。深度 10：2^10 = 1,024（大约一千）。顺着算：深度 20 是 2^20 = 1,048,576（大约一百万），深度 40 是 2^40，大约 1.1 万亿。这就是 p.27 说的指数增长（**exponential growth**）：层数只多了几倍，节点数却爆炸。（课件 p.27 只提了这个问题，没给数字，这些数是按“每层 ×2”的规律算出来的。）常见错误：算成 2 × 10 = 20；或者把深度 0 到 10 的所有节点加起来（2,047），而题目问的是“深度 10 这一层”。
explain.en: Nodes at depth d = 2^d, so depth 10 has 2^10 = 1,024 (about a thousand); depth 20 has about a million.

prompt.en: Discuss: In the Tic-Tac-Toe example, the state tree contains goal states where we (X) win. Does that mean we will win? Explain in 2-3 sentences.
prompt.zh: 讨论题：在井字棋（Tic-Tac-Toe）例子里，状态树中有我们（X）赢的目标状态。这是否意味着我们一定会赢？用 2–3 句英文解释。

modelAnswer.en: No. Unlike in single-player puzzles, we are no longer in control of every step of the game, because our opponent chooses their own moves and will try to block us. So finding a goal state no longer guarantees a win, and we need a version of Search that takes our opponent's goals into account, such as Minimax.
modelAnswer.zh: 先答 No；再给原因：我们不再控制每一步（对手自己选怎么走，会来堵我们）；最后点出结论和解决方法：找到目标状态不保证赢，需要一种考虑对手目标的搜索，也就是 Minimax。

points.en: No, it does not guarantee a win.
points.zh: 不，不保证赢

points.en: We are no longer in control of every step; the opponent chooses their own moves.
points.zh: 我们不再控制每一步，对手自己选走法

points.en: We need a version of Search that takes the opponent's goals into account (Minimax).
points.zh: 需要考虑对手目标的搜索（Minimax）

explain.zh: 这是 p.31 的 Discuss，答案在 p.32：Unlike in single-player puzzles, we are no longer in control of every step of the game. Finding a goal state no longer guarantees a win. 可以加上例子：p.31 的树里两个 Goal! 都要靠 O 不去堵才能走到，而理性的 O 会堵，所以 minimax 算出来根的值是 0（平局）。

prompt.en: According to the lecture, what does a rational agent do?
prompt.zh: 按课件，理性智能体（rational agent）会怎么做？

options.en: It always chooses actions that match human intentions, goals and ethics.
options.zh: 总是选择符合人类意图、目标和伦理的动作。

options.en: It always chooses actions that maximize the reward it will earn.
options.zh: 总是选择能让自己获得的奖励最大的动作。

options.en: It always chooses the action that ends the game as quickly as possible.
options.zh: 总是选择能最快结束游戏的动作。

options.en: It always chooses a random legal action.
options.zh: 总是随机选一个合法动作。

explain.zh: p.33：A rational agent always chooses actions that maximizes the reward it will earn.（课件原文把 maximize 写成了 maximizes，意思不变。）最容易混的是“符合人类意图、目标和伦理”：这是对齐（**Alignment**，p.64）希望做到的事，但理性智能体只看奖励，而奖励不一定和人类的价值观一致，这正是 p.64 提出的问题。“最快结束游戏”和“随机走”都不是课件的定义。
explain.en: p.33: a rational agent maximizes its reward. Matching human values is what Alignment aims for, and a rational agent does not guarantee it.

prompt.en: In a zero sum game, one possible outcome gives us a reward of +30. What reward does our opponent get for the same outcome?
prompt.zh: 在一个零和游戏（zero sum game）里，某个结局给我们的奖励是 +30。同一个结局，对手的奖励是多少？

explain.zh: p.33：In many games (called zero sum games), our opponent's reward is the negation of ours. “相反数（negation）”就是把正负号反过来：+30 → -30。两个人的奖励加起来正好是 0。常见错误：写 +30（以为两人一样）；写 70（用 100 - 30 算）；写 0。
explain.en: Zero sum: the opponent's reward is the negation of ours, so -30.

prompt.en: In the lecture's Tic-Tac-Toe example (we are X), two terminal states have a reward of +100, but minimax gives the root a value of 0. Why?
prompt.zh: 课件的井字棋例子里（我们是 X），有两个终止状态的奖励是 +100，但 minimax 算出根的值是 0。为什么？

options.en: Because minimax takes the average of all the terminal rewards in the tree
options.zh: 因为 minimax 取树里所有终止奖励的平均值

options.en: Because on our turn (X) we always choose the minimum value of the children
options.zh: 因为轮到我们（X）时，我们总是取孩子里的最小值

options.en: Because on O's turn, O picks the move that is worst for us and blocks our win
options.zh: 因为轮到 O 时，O 选对我们最不利的走法，堵住了我们

options.en: Because the two +100 states are not terminal states, so their values are ignored
options.zh: 因为 +100 的那两个状态不是终止状态，所以它们的值不算

explain.zh: 按 p.36–40 一步步算：最底下 6 个终止值是 +100, 0, 0, 0, 0, +100；X 在最后一步只有一种走法，值直接往上抄；轮到 O 时取最小：min(+100, 0) = 0，min(0, 0) = 0，min(0, +100) = 0；根轮到我们，取最大：max(0, 0, 0) = 0。+100 永远传不到根，因为理性的 O 会堵。p.40：If our opponent also plays rationally, the best result we can guarantee is a draw (reward of 0). 其他选项：取平均会得到 200 ÷ 6 ≈ 33.3，不是 0；我们（X）取的是最大值；+100 的棋盘上 X 已经赢了，游戏结束，当然是终止状态。
explain.en: O minimizes: min(+100, 0) = 0, min(0, 0) = 0, min(0, +100) = 0; then the root takes max(0, 0, 0) = 0, so the best we can guarantee is a draw.

prompt.en: Discuss: Minimax assumes that our opponent plays rationally. What reward might we get if our opponent doesn't play as expected? Use the Tic-Tac-Toe example in your answer.
prompt.zh: 讨论题：Minimax 假设对手理性地下棋。如果对手没有按预期下，我们可能得到什么奖励？用井字棋的例子回答。

modelAnswer.en: Minimax assumes that on the opponent's turn they always minimize our reward, so the root value is the reward we can guarantee if the opponent plays rationally. If the opponent does not play as expected, for example by making a mistake, we might get a higher reward. In the Tic-Tac-Toe example, the root value is 0 (a draw), but if O does not block our line, X can win and get +100.
modelAnswer.zh: 三句：① minimax 的假设（对手总让我们的奖励最小）；② 根的值是“对手理性时我们能保证的奖励”；③ 对手失误时我们可能拿得更多，例子：O 不堵，X 赢，得 +100（而不是平局 0）。

points.en: Minimax assumes the opponent always minimizes our reward.
points.zh: minimax 假设对手总让我们的奖励最小

points.en: The root value is the reward we can guarantee against a rational opponent (0 in Tic-Tac-Toe).
points.zh: 根的值 = 对手理性时我们能保证的奖励（井字棋是 0）

points.en: If the opponent makes a mistake, we might get more (X can win, +100).
points.zh: 对手失误时，我们可能拿得更多（X 能赢，+100）

explain.zh: 这是 p.41 的 Discuss，课件没给答案。关键是理解根的值是什么意思：它是在“对手每一步都下得最好”的假设下算出来的。p.40：If our opponent also plays rationally, the best result we can guarantee is a draw (reward of 0). 井字棋树里两个 +100 的结局，正好都要 O 不去堵才会出现。在这个例子里，O 不按预期走只会让 X 有机会赢，所以不要写成“我们会得到更少”。

prompt.en: Describe the Minimax algorithm at a high level and explain the role of heuristics. In your answer, mention terminal states, reward values, and what happens on our turn (▲) and on our opponent's turn (▼).
prompt.zh: 从整体上描述 Minimax 算法，并解释启发式（heuristics）起什么作用。答案里要提到终止状态、奖励值，以及轮到我们（▲）和轮到对手（▼）时分别怎么做。

modelAnswer.en: Minimax is a version of Search for two-player games that takes the opponent's goals into account. First, every terminal state is labelled with a reward value: a win is +100, a loss is -100 and a draw is 0. Then Minimax starts at the terminal states and carries values upwards, one level at a time. On our turn (▲), we choose the maximum value, because a rational agent maximizes its reward. On our opponent's turn (▼), they choose the minimum, because to maximize their own reward they must minimize ours. When a value reaches the root, we know which move to play and the reward we should get. However, many games have impossibly large state trees, so there is not enough time to reach the terminal states. Heuristics help here: we generate states to a fixed depth, score the bottom row with a heuristic, which estimates how good each state is, and run Minimax as if those states were terminal. The cost is that we lose the guarantees about the reward.
modelAnswer.zh: 结构：① minimax 是考虑对手目标的搜索；② 先给终止状态标奖励值（+100 / -100 / 0）；③ 从下往上传：▲ 取最大（理性智能体），▼ 取最小（对手要让自己最大，就得让我们最小）；④ 传到根 → 知道走哪一步、能得多少；⑤ 树太大 → 搜到固定深度，最底一排用启发式估分，当成终止状态做 minimax；⑥ 代价：失去对奖励的保证。

points.en: Terminal states are labelled with reward values (+100 win, -100 loss, 0 draw).
points.zh: 终止状态标奖励值（赢 +100、输 -100、平 0）

points.en: Values are carried upwards, starting from the terminal states.
points.zh: 从终止状态开始往上传值

points.en: Our turn (▲): take the maximum; opponent's turn (▼): take the minimum.
points.zh: ▲ 取最大，▼ 取最小

points.en: The root value tells us which move to play and the reward we should get.
points.zh: 根的值告诉我们走哪一步、能得多少

points.en: When the tree is too large, heuristics estimate the values of non-terminal states at a fixed depth.
points.zh: 树太大时，在固定深度用启发式估计非终止状态的值

points.en: Using heuristics loses the guarantees about the reward.
points.zh: 用启发式会失去对奖励的保证

explain.zh: 这题对应学习目标 4：Describe the Minimax algorithm at a high level and the role of heuristics。at a high level 的意思是讲清楚思路就行，不用写代码。必须出现的关键词：terminal states、carries values upwards、maximize / minimize、root、heuristic、fixed depth、estimate、lose guarantees。常见失分：把 ▲ 和 ▼ 说反；只讲 minimax，不讲启发式。

prompt.en: In the lecture's abstract minimax tree, the root is ▲ (our turn) and has two ▼ children. The left ▼ has two ▲ children: one with terminal values (2, 3) and one with terminal values (5, -9). The right ▼ has two ▲ children: one with terminal values (7, 5) and one with terminal values (0, -1). Using minimax, what is the value of the root?
prompt.zh: 课件的抽象 minimax 树：根是 ▲（轮到我们），有两个 ▼ 孩子。左边的 ▼ 有两个 ▲ 孩子，终止值分别是 (2, 3) 和 (5, -9)。右边的 ▼ 有两个 ▲ 孩子，终止值分别是 (7, 5) 和 (0, -1)。用 minimax 算，根的值是多少？

explain.zh:
从下往上，一层一层算（p.43–46）：
第 1 步，▲ 层取最大：max(2, 3) = 3；max(5, -9) = 5；max(7, 5) = 7；max(0, -1) = 0。
第 2 步，▼ 层取最小：左边 min(3, 5) = 3；右边 min(7, 0) = 0。
第 3 步，根 ▲ 取最大：max(3, 0) = 3，所以走左边（p.46：we should play the left move, whatever it is）。
常见错误：直接挑最大的叶子 7（对手不会让你拿到）；在 ▼ 层也取最大，也会得到 7；把 ▲ 和 ▼ 弄反。

prompt.en: In the lecture's abstract minimax tree, the root is ▲, its two children are ▼, and the terminal values from left to right are 2, 3, 5, -9, 7, 5, 0, -1 (two under each ▲ node). The largest terminal value, 7, is in the right half of the tree, but minimax tells us to play the left move. Why?
prompt.zh: 课件的抽象 minimax 树：根是 ▲，它的两个孩子是 ▼，终止值从左到右是 2, 3, 5, -9, 7, 5, 0, -1（每个 ▲ 下面两个）。最大的终止值 7 在树的右半边，但 minimax 让我们走左边。为什么？

options.en: The right ▼ would give min(7, 0) = 0, but the left ▼ gives min(3, 5) = 3.
options.zh: 右边的 ▼ 会得到 min(7, 0) = 0，而左边的 ▼ 得到 min(3, 5) = 3。

options.en: Minimax always prefers the left move whenever two moves look almost equally good.
options.zh: 两步看起来差不多好时，minimax 总是偏向左边。

options.en: The value 7 is only a heuristic estimate, so minimax does not trust it at all.
options.zh: 7 只是启发式估计值，minimax 根本不信它。

options.en: The root is a ▼ node, so at the root we take the minimum instead of the maximum.
options.zh: 根是 ▼ 节点，所以在根取最小值，而不是最大值。

explain.zh: minimax 的核心：不能只盯着“最好的那片叶子”，要假设对手会尽量让我们拿少。先算 ▲ 层：3, 5, 7, 0。右边的 ▼ 在 7 和 0 之间会选 0，左边的 ▼ 在 3 和 5 之间会选 3，3 比 0 大，所以走左边，预期奖励 3。其他选项：minimax 没有“偏左”的规则，p.46 说的是 the left move, whatever it is（不管左边那步具体是什么）；p.42 这棵树的底层是给定的终止值（Values of terminal states are given），不是启发式；根是 ▲（尖朝上，轮到我们取最大）。
explain.en: The opponent would steer the right branch to 0, while the left branch guarantees 3, so the root value is 3 and we play left.

prompt.en: Consider this abstract minimax tree, which has the same shape as the lecture's example: the root is ▲, it has two ▼ children, each ▼ has two ▲ children, and each ▲ has two terminal states. The terminal values from left to right are 6, -2, 4, 9, -5, 8, 1, 3. Using minimax, what is the value of the root?
prompt.zh: 看这棵抽象 minimax 树，形状和课件的例子一样：根是 ▲，有两个 ▼ 孩子；每个 ▼ 有两个 ▲ 孩子；每个 ▲ 有两个终止状态。终止值从左到右是 6, -2, 4, 9, -5, 8, 1, 3。用 minimax 算，根的值是多少？

explain.zh:
这是一棵练习用的新树（数字不是课件上的），方法和 p.43–46 完全一样：
第 1 步，▲ 层（两两一组取最大）：max(6, -2) = 6；max(4, 9) = 9；max(-5, 8) = 8；max(1, 3) = 3。
第 2 步，▼ 层取最小：左边 min(6, 9) = 6；右边 min(8, 3) = 3。
第 3 步，根 ▲ 取最大：max(6, 3) = 6，走左边。
常见错误：每层都取最大，得到 9；把 ▲ 和 ▼ 反过来做（▲ 取最小、▼ 取最大），得到 1。

prompt.en:
The lecture's minimax activity uses this abstract tree, where some nodes have only one child.
The root is ▲ (our turn) and has two ▼ children.
Left ▼: it has two ▲ children. The first ▲ has two ▼ children with terminal values (4, 3) and (0, 6). The second ▲ has only one ▼ child, with terminal values (1, 5).
Right ▼: it has only one ▲ child. That ▲ has two ▼ children with terminal values (5, 6) and (7, 9).
Using minimax, what is the value of the root?
prompt.zh:
课件的 minimax 课堂活动用的是下面这棵抽象树，其中有些节点只有一个孩子。
根是 ▲（轮到我们），有两个 ▼ 孩子。
左边的 ▼：有两个 ▲ 孩子。第一个 ▲ 有两个 ▼ 孩子，终止值分别是 (4, 3) 和 (0, 6)；第二个 ▲ 只有一个 ▼ 孩子，终止值是 (1, 5)。
右边的 ▼：只有一个 ▲ 孩子。这个 ▲ 有两个 ▼ 孩子，终止值分别是 (5, 6) 和 (7, 9)。
用 minimax 算，根的值是多少？

explain.zh:
从最底下往上，一层一层算（答案见 p.48–50）：
第 1 步，最底的 ▼ 取最小：min(4, 3) = 3；min(0, 6) = 0；min(1, 5) = 1；min(5, 6) = 5；min(7, 9) = 7。
第 2 步，▲ 取最大：max(3, 0) = 3；只有一个孩子的 ▲ 直接抄 1；max(5, 7) = 7。
第 3 步，根的两个 ▼ 孩子取最小：左边 min(3, 1) = 1；右边只有一个孩子，直接抄 7。
第 4 步，根 ▲ 取最大：max(1, 7) = 7，选右边（p.50：We should choose the right action!）。
常见错误：盯着最大的叶子 9（对手在 (7, 9) 那个 ▼ 会选 7）；每一层的 ▲ 和 ▼ 都弄反，会得到 5；在左边的 ▼ 取了 max(3, 1) = 3，这一步是错的（只是这棵树的根碰巧还是 7）。
explain.en: Bottom ▼: 3, 0, 1, 5, 7. ▲: 3, 1, 7. The root's ▼ children: min(3, 1) = 1 and 7. Root: max(1, 7) = 7, so we choose right.

prompt.en: In a minimax tree, a node that has only one child simply takes the value of that child, whether it is a ▲ node or a ▼ node.
prompt.zh: 在 minimax 树里，只有一个孩子的节点直接取那个孩子的值，不管它是 ▲ 还是 ▼。

explain.zh: 对。只有一个选择时，最大值和最小值都是它自己，所以直接往上抄。p.47 的活动树里有两个这样的节点：左边那个只有一个孩子的 ▲（抄 1），右边那个只有一个孩子的 ▼（抄 7）。井字棋例子 p.36 也是同样的道理：We have only one choice in each case… Copy these rewards up one level.
explain.en: True: with only one option, the maximum and the minimum are the same value.

prompt.en: According to the lecture, what is expert knowledge?
prompt.zh: 按课件，专家知识（expert knowledge）是什么？

options.en: Knowledge that a computer learns autonomously from data through Machine Learning
options.zh: 电脑通过机器学习从数据里自动学到的知识

options.en: The rules of a game, which tell us what actions can be taken in each state
options.zh: 游戏规则：告诉我们每个状态下能做哪些动作

options.en: The values of the terminal states at the bottom of a state tree
options.zh: 状态树最底下终止状态的值

options.en: The intuition and reasoning of human experts distilled for use by AI
options.zh: 把人类专家的直觉和推理提炼出来，交给 AI 使用

explain.zh: p.54：Expert knowledge is the intuition and reasoning of human experts distilled for use by AI. 同一页说启发式有两个来源：用机器学习自动学（learned autonomously through Machine Learning），或者用人类专家知识手工设计（crafted manually）。所以“从数据里自动学”恰好是另一条路，最容易选错；“游戏规则”是动态（**dynamics**）；“终止状态的值”是奖励值（**reward values**）。例子：国际象棋的子力优势就是专家知识（p.55）。
explain.en: p.54 definition. Learning from data is the Machine Learning route, the rules are the dynamics, and terminal values are reward values.

prompt.en: Which of the following statements about heuristics are correct according to the lecture? (Select all that apply.)
prompt.zh: 按课件，下面关于启发式（heuristics）的说法哪些正确？（多选）

options.en: A heuristic value can be greater than +100 if a position is very strong.
options.zh: 如果局面非常好，启发式的值可以超过 +100。

options.en: A heuristic is a numerical score for the 'goodness' of a state from our perspective.
options.zh: 启发式是从我们的角度，给一个状态的“好坏”打的数值分数。

options.en: Heuristics may be learned autonomously through Machine Learning.
options.zh: 启发式可以通过机器学习自动学出来。

options.en: When minimax relies on heuristics, the reward we will receive is still guaranteed.
options.zh: minimax 依赖启发式时，我们最后得到的奖励仍然有保证。

options.en: Heuristics are only useful for single-player puzzles.
options.zh: 启发式只对单人谜题有用。

options.en: Heuristics may be crafted manually, using human expert knowledge.
options.zh: 启发式可以用人类专家知识手工设计。

explain.zh: 正确的三句都是课件原话：定义（p.52）和两种来源（p.54）。错误的三句：超过 +100 不行，按奖励值的约定，保证赢才是 +100，其他情况必须在 -100 和 +100 之间（p.52）；依赖启发式会失去保证（p.58：we lose guarantees related to the reward），因为启发式只是估计；课件引入启发式正是为了多人游戏（p.51：multiplayer games can be complex and have impossibly large state trees），并不是只给单人谜题用。
explain.en: Correct: the p.52 definition and the two sources on p.54. Values must stay between -100 and +100, relying on heuristics loses the reward guarantees (p.58), and the lecture uses them for multiplayer games.

prompt.en: The lecture says chess material advantage is 'a simple, common format for a heuristic.' In this format, what are the features and what are the weights?
prompt.zh: 课件说国际象棋的子力优势是“启发式的一种简单、常见的格式”。在这种格式里，特征（features）是什么？权重（weights）是什么？

options.en: Features: the importance values 1, 3, 3, 5 and 9. Weights: how many of each piece each player has.
options.zh: 特征：表示重要性的 1、3、3、5、9。权重：每个玩家每种棋子的个数。

options.en: Features: how many of each piece each player has. Weights: the importance values 1, 3, 3, 5 and 9.
options.zh: 特征：每个玩家每种棋子的个数。权重：表示重要性的 1、3、3、5、9。

options.en: Features: the reward values +100, -100 and 0. Weights: the depths of the nodes in the state tree.
options.zh: 特征：奖励值 +100、-100、0。权重：状态树里节点的深度。

options.en: Features: the number of White's pieces only. Weights: the number of Black's pieces only.
options.zh: 特征：只算白方棋子的个数。权重：只算黑方棋子的个数。

explain.zh: p.55：A set of features (# pawns, # knights, etc.) is compared for each player, and their importance is weighted. 特征（**feature**）= 要数的东西（每种棋子的个数），每个特征都用“白方 - 黑方”来比；权重（**weight**）= 乘在前面、表示重要性的数（兵 1、马 3、象 3、车 5、后 9）。把两者对调是最常见的错误；奖励值和树的深度跟这个公式无关；公式里每一项都是白方和黑方相减，不是一方算特征、另一方算权重。
explain.en: Features are the piece counts compared for each player (# White minus # Black); weights are the importance values 1, 3, 3, 5 and 9.

prompt.en:
Use the material advantage heuristic from the lecture:
`Material Advantage = 1*[(# W pawns) - (# B pawns)] + 3*[(# W knights) - (# B knights)] + 3*[(# W bishops) - (# B bishops)] + 5*[(# W rooks) - (# B rooks)] + 9*[(# W queens) - (# B queens)]`
White has 6 pawns, 2 knights, 1 bishop, 2 rooks and 1 queen. Black has 6 pawns, 1 knight, 2 bishops, 1 rook and 0 queens. What is the material advantage?
prompt.zh:
用课件的子力优势（material advantage）公式：
子力优势 = 1 ×（白兵 - 黑兵）+ 3 ×（白马 - 黑马）+ 3 ×（白象 - 黑象）+ 5 ×（白车 - 黑车）+ 9 ×（白后 - 黑后）
白方：6 个兵、2 个马、1 个象、2 个车、1 个后。黑方：6 个兵、1 个马、2 个象、1 个车、0 个后。子力优势是多少？

explain.zh:
逐项算，永远是“白 - 黑”，再乘权重：
兵（pawn）：1 × (6 - 6) = 0
马（knight）：3 × (2 - 1) = 3
象（bishop）：3 × (1 - 2) = -3
车（rook）：5 × (2 - 1) = 5
后（queen）：9 × (1 - 0) = 9
合计：0 + 3 - 3 + 5 + 9 = 14，白方占优。
说明：这是练习用的新局面（数字不是课件上的）；课件 p.53 那个棋盘的算法见讲解第 15 节（结果 +3）。
常见错误：减反了（黑 - 白），得到 -14；忘了乘权重，得到 0 + 1 - 1 + 1 + 1 = 2。

prompt.en: According to the lecture, heuristics don't give a full picture of the game state, and they may not always be accurate.
prompt.zh: 按课件：启发式不能完整反映游戏状态，也不一定总是准确。

explain.zh: 对。p.56 原话：Heuristics don't give a full picture of the game state, and may not always be accurate. 同一页还说：A good heuristic should rank states from best to worst as accurately as possible（好的启发式应该尽可能准确地把状态从最好排到最差）。比如子力优势只数棋子个数，不看棋子站在哪里，所以只是一种估计。
explain.en: True (p.56). A good heuristic should rank states from best to worst as accurately as possible.

prompt.en: To make sure minimax does not run out of time in a game with a very large state tree, what does the lecture suggest?
prompt.zh: 在状态树非常大的游戏里，为了让 minimax 不超时，课件建议怎么做？

options.en: Generate the whole tree to the end of the game, but only draw our own moves, not the opponent's
options.zh: 把整棵树生成到游戏结束，但只画我们自己的走法，不画对手的

options.en: Stop as soon as any goal state is found, just as we did in a single-player puzzle
options.zh: 像在单人谜题里那样，一找到目标状态就停

options.en: Search to a fixed depth, score the bottom row with a heuristic, then use Minimax on those values
options.zh: 只搜到固定深度，用启发式给最底一排打分，再对这些值做 minimax

options.en: Use heuristic values for every node in the tree instead of carrying values up with minimax
options.zh: 树里每个节点都直接用启发式值，不再用 minimax 往上传值

explain.zh: p.57 原话：to ensure we don't run out of time, we can generate states to a fixed depth and calculate heuristic values for the bottom row. Then we can use Minimax, as if they were terminal states. 其他选项：只生成自己的走法就没有考虑对手，不是 minimax；多人游戏里找到目标状态不保证赢（p.32），不能一找到就停；启发式只给最底一排（固定深度处）打分，上面各层仍然用 max / min 往上传，不是每个节点都用启发式。代价是：启发式只是估计，所以会失去对奖励的保证（p.58）。
explain.en: p.57: search to a fixed depth, score the bottom row with a heuristic, and run Minimax as if those states were terminal.

prompt.en: Explain the guarantees given by Search and the difficulties in finding solutions. Compare (1) exhaustive search in a single-player puzzle, (2) minimax in a two-player game, and (3) minimax that stops at a fixed depth and uses heuristics.
prompt.zh: 解释搜索（Search）能给出哪些保证，以及找解有哪些难点。请比较：(1) 单人谜题里的穷举搜索；(2) 两人游戏里的 minimax；(3) 搜到固定深度、使用启发式的 minimax。

modelAnswer.en: In a single-player puzzle, exhaustive search gives a strong guarantee: when it finds a goal state, the path of actions from the root to that goal state is a solution that is guaranteed to be correct. The difficulty is that the number of nodes grows exponentially with depth and each state generated costs time, so if no goal state is found in time, we must give up with no solution. In a two-player game, finding a goal state no longer guarantees a win, because we do not control the opponent's moves. Minimax assumes that we maximize and the opponent minimizes our reward, so the root value is the reward we can guarantee if the opponent also plays rationally, for example a draw (0) in Tic-Tac-Toe. However, game trees can be impossibly large, so we may stop at a fixed depth and score the bottom row with heuristics. Since heuristics are only estimates, we lose the guarantees about the reward, but estimates are better than nothing.
modelAnswer.zh: 按三种情况分段写，每种都说“能保证什么 + 难在哪”：① 单人谜题：解保证正确；难点是节点数指数增长，时间不够只能放弃；② 两人游戏：找到目标状态不保证赢；minimax 在对手也理性时能保证根的值（井字棋 = 平局 0）；③ 树太大：固定深度 + 启发式，失去保证，但总比什么都没有好。

points.en: Single-player: the path from the root to a goal state is guaranteed to be correct.
points.zh: 单人谜题：根到目标状态的路径保证正确

points.en: Difficulty: the number of nodes grows exponentially with depth; we may have to give up with no solution.
points.zh: 难点：节点数指数增长，可能只能放弃、没有解

points.en: Two-player: finding a goal state no longer guarantees a win (we cannot control the opponent).
points.zh: 两人游戏：找到目标状态不再保证赢（控制不了对手）

points.en: Minimax guarantees the root value if the opponent plays rationally (a draw, 0, in Tic-Tac-Toe).
points.zh: minimax：对手理性时保证根的值（井字棋为平局 0）

points.en: Fixed depth with heuristics: heuristics are estimates, so we lose the guarantees, but estimates are better than nothing.
points.zh: 固定深度 + 启发式：只是估计，失去保证，但比什么都没有好

explain.zh: 这题对应学习目标 3：Explain the guarantees given by Search and the difficulties in finding solutions。“保证（guarantee）”是整课的主线：p.5（provably correct when they are found）、p.26（guaranteed to be correct）、p.32（no longer guarantees a win）、p.40（the best result we can guarantee is a draw）、p.58（we lose guarantees）。按三种情况分段写最清楚。常见失分：只写“搜索很慢”，没说明为什么慢（指数增长），也没说丢了什么保证。

prompt.en: A computer is given the rules of Sokoban. It must find a sequence of moves that solves a new level and then carry out those moves. Using the lecture's terms, which approach is this, and where is most of the time usually spent?
prompt.zh: 电脑拿到推箱子的规则，要自己找出能解开一个新关卡的走法序列，再把这些走法执行出来。用课件的说法，这属于哪种方法？时间通常主要花在哪里？

options.en: Symbolic AI; most of the time is usually spent searching for the solution
options.zh: 符号 AI；时间通常主要花在搜索（找）解上

options.en: Symbolic AI; most of the time is usually spent executing the moves
options.zh: 符号 AI；时间通常主要花在执行走法上

options.en: Pure Algorithm; most of the time is usually spent searching for the solution
options.zh: 纯算法；时间通常主要花在找解上

options.en: Pure Algorithm; most of the time is usually spent executing the moves
options.zh: 纯算法；时间通常主要花在执行走法上

explain.zh: p.62：Symbolic AI: We specify a way to find a solution, the computer then finds and executes the solution。这里人只给了规则（也就是找解的方法），解是电脑自己找的，所以是符号 AI。p.63：Symbolic AI: Solutions are usually fast to execute, but finding them can take a long time，而且课件举的正是推箱子：Compare the process of executing a solution in Sokoban to the Search process needed to find that solution. 纯算法（**Pure Algorithm**）是人直接把解写好、电脑照着做（We specify the solution, the computer just follows it），时间只取决于执行；这里的解不是人写好的，所以不是纯算法。
explain.en: We only give a way to find the solution, so it is Symbolic AI (p.62); executing is fast, but finding the solution can take a long time (p.63).

prompt.en: In a Pure Algorithm, we specify a way to find a solution, and the computer then finds and executes the solution.
prompt.zh: 纯算法（Pure Algorithm）里，我们给出找解的方法，电脑再自己找到解并执行。

explain.zh: 错。这句描述的是符号 AI。p.62 原话：Pure Algorithm: We specify the solution, the computer just follows it. 以及 Symbolic AI: We specify a way to find a solution, the computer then finds and executes the solution. 区别就在于：人给的是“解本身”，还是“找解的方法”。时间上（p.63）：纯算法通常很快，只取决于执行解要多久；符号 AI 执行很快，但找解可能很久。
explain.en: False: that sentence describes Symbolic AI. In a Pure Algorithm we specify the solution and the computer just follows it.

prompt.en: In the lecture's shared pasture example, rewards are written as (our reward, neighbour's reward). After we choose 'sustainable', the neighbour can choose between (2,2) and (0,3). The neighbour picks overgraze, giving (0,3). Why?
prompt.zh: 课件的共享牧场例子里，奖励写成（我们的奖励，邻居的奖励）。我们选了 sustainable（可持续放牧）之后，邻居可以在 (2,2) 和 (0,3) 之间选。邻居选了 overgraze（过度放牧），得到 (0,3)。为什么？

options.en: Because the neighbour wants to minimize our reward, as in a zero sum game
options.zh: 因为邻居想让我们的奖励最小，就像零和游戏那样

options.en: Because the neighbour maximizes their own reward (3 > 2) and does not care about ours
options.zh: 因为邻居让自己的奖励最大（3 比 2 大），不在乎我们的奖励

options.en: Because overgrazing here gives the best result for both of the farmers
options.zh: 因为这里过度放牧对两个农夫都是最好的结果

options.en: Because the neighbour wants the largest total reward for both farmers
options.zh: 因为邻居想让两个农夫的奖励总和最大

explain.zh: p.65 原话：The neighbouring farmer doesn't want to minimize your reward, but also doesn't care about it in the pursuit of their own reward. 邻居只看括号里的第二个数：(2,2) 给他 2，(0,3) 给他 3，3 比 2 大，所以选过度放牧。“想让我们最小”正是课件特意否定的说法（这个游戏也不是零和游戏）；(0,3) 让我们只拿 0，显然不是“对两人都最好”；如果邻居想让两人的总奖励最大，他会选 (2,2)（总共 4），而不是 (0,3)（总共 3）。
explain.en: p.65: the neighbour does not try to minimize our reward; they simply maximize their own (3 is more than 2).

prompt.en: In the lecture's shared pasture example, rewards are written as (our reward, neighbour's reward): both graze sustainably (2,2); we graze sustainably and the neighbour overgrazes (0,3); we overgraze and the neighbour grazes sustainably (3,0); both overgraze (1,1). We choose first, then the neighbour chooses. What outcome does minimax predict, and what does this show about alignment?
prompt.zh: 课件的共享牧场例子，奖励写成（我们的奖励，邻居的奖励）：都可持续放牧 (2,2)；我们可持续、邻居过度放牧 (0,3)；我们过度放牧、邻居可持续 (3,0)；都过度放牧 (1,1)。我们先选，邻居后选。minimax 预测的结果是什么？这说明了对齐（alignment）的什么问题？

modelAnswer.en: The neighbour always overgrazes (3 > 2 and 1 > 0), so we choose between (0,3) and (1,1) and also overgraze (1 > 0). The result is (1,1), even though (2,2) was better for both farmers. This shows that rational agents that only maximize their own reward can reach an outcome that is worse for everyone, so the reward is not aligned with what we really value.
modelAnswer.zh: ① 邻居那一层：3 比 2 大、1 比 0 大，所以邻居总是过度放牧，我们面对的是 (0,3) 或 (1,1)；② 我们那一层：1 比 0 大，选过度放牧，结果 (1,1)；③ 但 (2,2) 对两人都更好；④ 说明：只追求自己奖励的理性智能体，结果可能对所有人都更差，奖励和我们真正看重的价值没有对齐。

points.en: The neighbour overgrazes in both branches (3 is more than 2, and 1 is more than 0).
points.zh: 邻居两种情况都选过度放牧（3 比 2 大，1 比 0 大）

points.en: We compare 0 with 1 and also overgraze, so the result is (1,1).
points.zh: 我们比较 0 和 1，也选过度放牧，结果是 (1,1)

points.en: (2,2) would have been better for both farmers.
points.zh: (2,2) 本来对两个农夫都更好

points.en: Rational agents that maximize only their own reward can produce outcomes that do not match our values (an alignment problem).
points.zh: 只顾自己奖励的理性智能体，结果可能不符合我们的价值观（对齐问题）

explain.zh: 推理过程见 p.66–69，结论是 p.69 的原话：We end up choosing to overgraze, even though there was an option better for both farmers. 注意这里 ▼ 那一层不是“让我们最小”，而是邻居让自己的奖励最大（p.65）。课件用这个例子说明：理性智能体追求自己的奖励，但这个奖励不一定符合人类真正看重的东西（p.64）。

prompt.en: Activity: Think of an example in the real world where a mismatch in alignment between reward and values (yours or society's) is causing real problems. Describe the scenario and its consequences, and suggest possible solutions to the misalignment.
prompt.zh: 课堂活动：举一个现实世界的例子，说明“奖励”和（你个人或社会的）价值观没有对齐，正在造成真实的问题。描述情境和后果，并提出可能的解决办法。

modelAnswer.en: Alignment is the problem of trying to make AI behaviour match human values. One example of misalignment is a food delivery platform whose system is rewarded for making delivery times as short as possible. This reward is easy to measure, but it does not match everything society values, such as the safety and fair treatment of delivery riders. As a result, riders may feel pushed to rush and take risks in traffic, which can put them and other people on the road in danger. Like a rational agent, the system does what maximizes its reward, not what we really want. To fix this misalignment, the reward could also include safety and rider wellbeing, not only speed. The platform could also add rules or limits, such as more realistic delivery times. Finally, humans should regularly check the real outcomes and correct the system when it causes harm.
modelAnswer.zh: 结构：① 一句话定义 alignment（p.64）；② 情境：系统的奖励是什么（这里是“送得越快越好”）；③ 奖励和价值观哪里不一致（骑手的安全和公平对待）；④ 后果（骑手赶时间、在路上冒险，危及自己和路人）；⑤ 联系理性智能体：系统只让奖励最大；⑥ 解决办法：修改奖励（加入安全）、加规则限制、人来检查和纠正。

points.en: Defines alignment: making AI behaviour match human values.
points.zh: 定义对齐：让 AI 的行为符合人类的价值观

points.en: Gives a concrete real-world scenario and names the reward that is being maximized.
points.zh: 给出具体的现实情境，并说清被最大化的奖励是什么

points.en: Explains the mismatch between the reward and the values (yours or society's).
points.zh: 说明奖励和（个人或社会的）价值观哪里不一致

points.en: Describes the real consequences of the misalignment.
points.zh: 描述它造成的真实后果

points.en: Suggests possible solutions, such as changing the reward, adding rules, or human oversight.
points.zh: 提出解决办法：修改奖励、加规则、人工监督等

explain.zh: 这是 p.71 的课堂活动和讨论题，没有标准答案，只要例子合理、结构完整就能得分。也可以换别的例子，比如推荐视频的系统只追求观看时长，结果推荐偏激或误导的内容（本课讲解里用的例子）。写的时候一定要点名“奖励是什么”和“价值观是什么”，再说两者哪里不一致，否则容易写成泛泛的“AI 有风险”。

prompt.en: Which of the following is NOT one of the sub-fields of Symbolic AI listed in the lecture?
prompt.zh: 下面哪一项不是课件列出的符号 AI 子领域？

options.en: Search
options.zh: 搜索

options.en: Constraint Satisfaction
options.zh: 约束满足

options.en: Bayesian Reasoning
options.zh: 贝叶斯推理

options.en: Supervised Learning
options.zh: 监督学习

explain.zh: p.7 列了符号 AI 的四个子领域：Search（搜索）、Constraint Satisfaction（约束满足）、Logical Reasoning（逻辑推理）、Bayesian Reasoning（贝叶斯推理），本课只讲 Search。监督学习（**Supervised Learning**）是 Lecture 1 讲的机器学习的一种，靠数据学习，不是符号 AI 的子领域。易错点：贝叶斯推理这个名字你可能没见过，但它确实是 p.7 列出的子领域之一。
explain.en: p.7 lists Search, Constraint Satisfaction, Logical Reasoning and Bayesian Reasoning. Supervised Learning is a type of Machine Learning (Lecture 1).

prompt.en: In the state tree activity, the goal state is reached from the root by the actions up, right, down. What is the depth of the goal state?
prompt.zh: 状态树活动里，从根经过 up、right、down 到达目标状态。目标状态的深度是多少？

explain.zh: p.21：The depth of a node is the number of edges between it and the root. 深度 = 和根之间隔着几条边。up、right、down 每个动作是一条边，共 3 条，所以深度是 3（p.25 的 Goal! 在最底下一排，就是深度 3）。常见错误：数节点（根、up 之后、right 之后、Goal!）得到 4；以为根的深度是 1，也会多算 1。
explain.en: Depth is the number of edges between the node and the root: up, right and down are 3 edges, so the depth is 3.

prompt.en: In a game where 3 actions are possible from every state, how many nodes are at depth 4 of the state tree? (The root is at depth 0.)
prompt.zh: 在一个游戏里，每个状态都有 3 个可做的动作。状态树的深度 4 这一层有多少个节点？（根在深度 0。）

explain.zh:
这是用新数字练习 p.27 的“每层乘一个固定倍数”（指数增长）：课件的树每层乘 2，这里每层乘 3。
深度 0：1
深度 1：1 × 3 = 3
深度 2：3 × 3 = 9
深度 3：9 × 3 = 27
深度 4：27 × 3 = 81（也就是 3^4 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3）
常见错误：算成 3 × 4 = 12（应该是 4 个 3 相乘，不是 3 乘 4）；把深度 0 到 4 全加起来，1 + 3 + 9 + 27 + 81 = 121（题目只问深度 4 这一层）。
explain.en: Each level multiplies the count by 3: 1, 3, 9, 27, 81. So depth 4 has 3^4 = 81 nodes.

prompt.en:
Consider this abstract minimax tree. The root is ▲ (our turn) and has three ▼ children.
The left ▼ has two terminal states, with values 4 and -2.
The middle ▼ has only one terminal state, with value 6.
The right ▼ has three terminal states, with values -5, 9 and 1.
Using minimax, what is the value of the root?
prompt.zh:
看这棵抽象 minimax 树。根是 ▲（轮到我们），有三个 ▼ 孩子。
左边的 ▼ 下面有两个终止状态，值是 4 和 -2。
中间的 ▼ 下面只有一个终止状态，值是 6。
右边的 ▼ 下面有三个终止状态，值是 -5、9 和 1。
用 minimax 算，根的值是多少？

explain.zh:
这是一棵练习用的新树（数字不是课件上的），而且不整齐：三个 ▼ 分别有 2 个、1 个、3 个孩子。
第 1 步，三个 ▼ 取最小：左边 min(4, -2) = -2；中间只有一个孩子，直接抄 6；右边 min(-5, 9, 1) = -5。
第 2 步，根 ▲ 取最大：max(-2, 6, -5) = 6，所以走中间那一步。
常见错误：直接挑最大的叶子 9，或者在 ▼ 层也取最大，都会得到 9（右边的 ▼ 会把它压到 -5）；负数比大小弄错（-5 比 -2 小，因为数轴上越往左越小）。
explain.en: ▼ values: min(4, -2) = -2, 6 (only one child) and min(-5, 9, 1) = -5. Root: max(-2, 6, -5) = 6.

prompt.en: A goal test gives a T/F result for any state we give it.
prompt.zh: 对给它的任何状态，目标测试（goal test）都给出一个 T/F 的结果。

explain.zh: 对。p.18 原话：A goal test gives a T/F result for any state we give it. T/F 就是 True/False（真/假）：目标测试只回答“这个状态赢了没有”。让它给出 T 的状态叫目标状态（**goal state**）。注意它不打分：-100 到 +100 的数字是后面的奖励值（reward values）和启发式（heuristics）。
explain.en: True (p.18). States where the goal test gives T are called goal states.

prompt.en: If enough time passes and no goal state is found, exhaustive search eventually has to give up with no solution.
prompt.zh: 如果过了足够长的时间还没找到目标状态，穷举搜索最后只能放弃，没有解。

explain.zh: 对。p.28 原话：If enough time passes and no goal state is found, we eventually have to give up with no solution. 原因是节点数随深度指数增长，每生成一个状态都要花时间（p.27）。这也提醒我们：符号 AI 保证的是“找到的解是对的”（provably correct when they are found），不保证一定能找到解。
explain.en: True (p.28). Because of exponential growth, we may run out of time before a goal state is found.

prompt.en: Compare a Pure Algorithm with Symbolic AI. What do we specify in each, and where is the time usually spent?
prompt.zh: 比较纯算法（Pure Algorithm）和符号 AI（Symbolic AI）：两者分别由我们给出什么？时间通常花在哪里？

modelAnswer.en: In a Pure Algorithm, we specify the solution and the computer just follows it, so it is usually fast and the time depends entirely on how long the solution takes to execute. In Symbolic AI, we specify a way to find a solution, and the computer finds and executes the solution. The solution is usually fast to execute, but finding it can take a long time, for example when searching for a Sokoban solution.
modelAnswer.zh: 两边各写两点：纯算法 = 我们给出解 + 时间只取决于执行；符号 AI = 我们给出找解的方法 + 执行快、找解可能很慢（例子：搜索推箱子的解）。

points.en: Pure Algorithm: we specify the solution, and the computer just follows it.
points.zh: 纯算法：我们给出解，电脑照着执行

points.en: Pure Algorithm: usually fast; the time depends on how long the solution takes to execute.
points.zh: 纯算法：通常很快，时间取决于执行解要多久

points.en: Symbolic AI: we specify a way to find a solution; the computer finds and executes it.
points.zh: 符号 AI：我们给出找解的方法，电脑自己找到解再执行

points.en: Symbolic AI: executing is usually fast, but finding the solution can take a long time.
points.zh: 符号 AI：执行通常很快，但找解可能很久

explain.zh: p.62–63 的原话。答题顺序：先写“我们给什么、电脑做什么”（p.62），再写“时间花在哪”（p.63），最后可以举推箱子的例子：照着 up, right, down 走一遍很快，但搜索出这串动作要生成状态树（p.63：Compare the process of executing a solution in Sokoban to the Search process needed to find that solution）。常见失分：把两边说反；只写“符号 AI 慢”，没说慢在“找解”而不是“执行解”。

prompt.en: Lecture 1 says that Symbolic AI solutions are 'provably correct when they are found', while Machine Learning solutions are 'likely correct, but not guaranteed to be correct'. Compare the guarantees given by (a) exhaustive search in a single-player puzzle, (b) full minimax in a two-player game, (c) minimax with heuristics at a fixed depth, and (d) a trained Machine Learning model.
prompt.zh: Lecture 1 说符号 AI 的解“找到时可证明是正确的”，而机器学习的解“很可能正确，但不保证正确”。比较下面四种情况给出的保证：(a) 单人谜题里的穷举搜索；(b) 两人游戏里完整的 minimax；(c) 固定深度 + 启发式的 minimax；(d) 训练好的机器学习模型。

modelAnswer.en: Symbolic AI solutions are provably correct when they are found, but the strength of the guarantee depends on the method. (a) In a single-player puzzle, when exhaustive search finds a goal state, the path of actions from the root to the goal state is guaranteed to be correct, because we control every step. However, if no goal state is found in time, we must give up with no solution. (b) In a two-player game, full minimax carries the true rewards of the terminal states up to the root, so we know the reward we can guarantee if our opponent also plays rationally; in Tic-Tac-Toe, that is a draw. (c) With a fixed depth, the bottom-row values are only heuristic estimates, so we lose the guarantees about the reward we will receive, although estimates are better than nothing. (d) A trained ML model gives solutions that are likely correct, but not guaranteed to be correct.
modelAnswer.zh: 得分结构：按四种情况分四段写（③ 和 ④ 都没有保证）：① 单人穷举搜索：找到目标状态，路径一定是正确的解（p.26）；但时间用完可能没有解（p.28）；② 完整 minimax：值从真实的终止状态传上来，对手也理性时能保证根的值（井字棋保证平局，p.40–41）；③ 固定深度 + 启发式：最底一排只是估计，失去对奖励的保证（p.58）；④ 机器学习：大概率正确，但不保证（Lecture 1 p.52）。

points.en: Exhaustive search in a single-player puzzle: a found solution is guaranteed to be correct (but search may give up with no solution).
points.zh: 单人谜题的穷举搜索：找到的解保证正确（但可能找不到、只能放弃）。

points.en: Full minimax: if the opponent also plays rationally, the best result we can guarantee is the root value (e.g. a draw in Tic-Tac-Toe).
points.zh: 完整 minimax：如果对手也理性，我们能保证的最好结果就是根的值（如井字棋的平局）。

points.en: Fixed depth with heuristics: heuristics are only estimates, so we lose the guarantees about the reward.
points.zh: 固定深度 + 启发式：启发式只是估计，所以失去对奖励的保证。

points.en: Machine Learning: solutions are likely correct, but not guaranteed to be correct.
points.zh: 机器学习：解大概率正确，但不保证正确。

explain.zh: 跨课题：Lecture 1 p.48、p.52 和 Lecture 3 p.5、p.26、p.28、p.40–41、p.58。“provably correct when they are found” 指搜索真正走到了目标 / 终止状态、按规则推出的解；一旦最底下用启发式“估”分，就不再有这个保证。常见丢分：说“符号 AI 永远保证正确”（固定深度 + 启发式就没有保证）；说完整 minimax 无论对手怎么走都保证赢（课件只说对手也理性时，我们能保证根的值）。
explain.en: Links Lecture 1 p.48 and p.52 with Lecture 3 p.26, p.28, p.40-41 and p.58.
